sentences.text: Revenue rose from $41.9 billion in FY2016 [F1] to $47.9 billion in FY2025 [F10], a 1.5% CAGR [F219], while net income compounded at 8.1% [F222].
FY2017 is the first step change: net income fell 80.9% to $1.25 billion [D44][F52], which the filing ties to North America refranchising charges in other income [P53][X92].
FY2018 operating margin rose to 26.7% from 21.4% [F43][F42], but revenue for both years was recast, so the step is not like-for-like [F2][X2][F3][X3].
FY2025 operating margin reached 28.7% [F50], the window high [D765], on a 37.7% rise in operating income [D450] that laps prior-year charges [P12].
Revenue rose 1.9% to $47.9 billion in FY2025 from $47.1 billion [D449][F10][F9].
Concentrate operations supplied 1.6pp of that growth and 59.4% of revenue, the largest single driver [D534][D532].
The 10-K cites worldwide concentrate volume growth of 1% as the volume driver [P16][D534].
Operating income rose 37.7% [D450] on revenue growth of 1.9% [D449], a gap the 10-K ties mainly to lower other operating charges [P12].
Diluted EPS rose 23.6% against 23.3% for net income [D453][D451], as diluted shares fell 0.2% [D468].
Operating margin of 28.7% is the window high [F50][D765], 2.7pp above the 26.0% window median [D766].
Of the 7.5pp gain in FY2025 [D463], 6.2pp came from other lines [D477], which the 10-K ties to lower other operating charges after the fairlife remeasurement [P12].
Cost of revenue added 0.6pp [D475] and SG&A 0.7pp [D476], so the residual did most of the work.
Gross margin rose 0.6pp to 61.6% [D462][F30] on pricing and the prior-year refranchising, offset by currency and commodity costs [P14].
Net margin of 27.3% [F70] sits 1.4pp below operating margin [F50], and the filing attributes the 17.9% tax rate [D435] partly to incentive grants worth $383 million [P2].
Free cash flow of $5.30 billion [F120] was 0.40x net income [D437], the window low [D776] against a 0.97x median [D778].
Operating cash flow fell 41.3% to $6.81 billion in FY2024 [D404][F99], driven by a $6.0 billion IRS tax litigation deposit [P22].
Operating cash flow recovered 8.9% to $7.41 billion in FY2025 [D454][F100], which the filing ties mainly to lower tax payments and working-capital timing [P1].
Capex at 2.01x D&A [D438], up from 1.27x in FY2016 [D11], is a drag, holding FCF margin at 11.0% [D433] against a 20.2% window median [D775].

Net cash was $8.78 billion in FY2025 [D442], but FY2024 and FY2025 debt equals short-term borrowings only [D391][D441][X185][X186], so it is not comparable with FY2023's net debt of $32.4 billion [D341].
Against six staples peers, net cash ranks at the 100th percentile [D793], with a peer median of -14.5% of revenue [D794], but that ranking uses the same debt input.
The current ratio of 1.46x [F200] is the window high [D780], with working capital of $9.76 billion [F190].
Buybacks of $746 million and dividends of $8.78 billion totalled $9.53 billion [X135][X145][D444], 179.9% of FCF [D445]; diluted shares fell 0.2% [D468].
FY2017 and FY2018 revenue were recast upward: $36.2 billion against $35.4 billion first reported [F2][X2], and $34.3 billion against $31.9 billion [F3][X3] [R1].
Buybacks plus dividends exceeded FCF in FY2023 to FY2025, reaching 179.9% in FY2025 [R2][D445].
FCF also ran below 80% of net income in FY2024 and FY2025, at 0.45x and 0.40x [R3][D387][D437].
Currency cut consolidated operating income by 12% in FY2025 [P11], with Latin America down to $3.74 billion from $3.79 billion [S60][S59][P9].
The 10-K flags a trademark with $2.44 billion of remaining carrying value and warns of a further impairment if results miss revised projections [P20].
A fall toward the 26.0% window median [D766] from 28.7% [F50] would confirm the FY2025 step-up was mostly lapped charges [P12]; check the FY2026 10-K.
FCF to net income above the 0.97x window median [D778] would signal recovery, while a print near the 0.40x window low [D776] would extend the trend [D437]; watch the FY2026 10-K.
Payouts above the FY2023 level of 105.1% of FCF [D344], from 179.9% in FY2025 [D445], would confirm the gap persists; check the FY2026 cash flow statement.
